players.note: Budda Baker has been excellent this season, most recently tabulating two solos, three assists, one interception, and two passes defended. Budda's spike week comes one week after his first splash week of the season, making it evident that Baker is currently in top-15 mode. Budda, of course, is playing either for a new contract or to force the Cardinals to keep him rostered past the start of the 2027 league year. Budda has no guaranteed money left on his deal and is playing like it. Tap Baker as a top-15 option going forward; he is going to be motivated all season.

Evan Williams has been one of the biggest surprises of the IDP season. The DB1 through four weeks of action, Williams finished Week 4 with three solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Williams has two splash weeks and two spike weeks to his name and needs to be counted as a DB1 play until he cools down. Fire him up as a top-12 option for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Nick Emmanwori stepped up in Week 4, posting eight solos, one assist, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Emmanwori recorded his first spike week of the season and looks like he is ready to reclaim top-five status at the position. Tap him as a top-10 play for a plus Week 5 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Jalen Pitre showed up in Week 4, registering seven solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Pitre has recorded four or more solos in two of his four contests, settling him in as more of a back-end DB2 than the elite option some may have hoped for. He remains a top-25 option weekly and should be treated as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Xavier Watts was at it again in Week 4, racking up five solos, three assists, and 0.5 sacks. Watts has registered three consecutive spike weeks, locking him as a top-20 option until he cools down. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the banged-up Baltimore Ravens.

Cooper DeJean stepped up in Week 4, racking up three solos, two assists, one interception, and two passes defended. It was the first spike week for Cooper, who has topped three solo tackles just once all season. Drop DeJean down to the low-end DB3/CB2 realm until he starts to show some consistency. We all know the talent and upside is there, so he remains a DB3 option, but lower your expectations until he starts producing at a level commensurate with the DB2 he was expected to be.

Kamari Lassiter was at it again in Week 4, notching seven solos, one assist, and two passes defended. Kamari has posted back-to-back spike weeks, solidifying him as a top-30 option. The DB16 in total fantasy points, Lassiter is a corner who is fed a steady diet of tackle production due to playing across from Derek Stingley Jr. Tap Kamari as a DB3 with DB2 upside for Week 5 and beyond.

Christian Izien was excellent in Week 4, racking up seven solos, four assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Izien looked like an elite IDP force in his two starts, posting two splash weeks. The splash weeks put him as the DB1 in fantasy points per game and the DB15 in overall fantasy points despite making just two starts since being called up from the practice squad in Week 2 (he played five percent of the snaps against Buffalo that week). Izien could have one more start in him, but Brian Branch has returned to limited sessions for the Detroit Lions. He is expected to see his snaps managed if he suits up this weekend, but Izien will likely be the one leaving the field when Branch takes his snaps. And if Branch is deemed healthy enough to play, you have to imagine that he would be ready for at least a 50 percent snap share, or the Lions would probably just choose to sit him out another week. Izien is a start if Branch is ruled out by Friday, but should remain on fantasy benches if Branch is active.

Devon Witherspoon showed up in Week 4, tallying eight solos, one assist, and one tackle for loss. It was the first spike week for Witherspoon, who had been right on the cusp in two of his previous three weeks. Devon has established himself as a locked-in CB1/DB3 play due to his tackle production. The Seahawks corner has registered four or more solos in three straight games. Tap Witherspoon as a top-36 DB option for a tasty Week 5 matchup against the banged-up San Francisco 49ers.

Minkah returned with a bang in Week 4, tallying eight solos, eight assists, one interception, and one pass defended. He played 100 percent of the snaps in his first game back from a groin injury, and his performance suggests that he is safe to be counted as a top-15 option immediately. Dane Belton took the snap hit with Fitzpatrick returning. Tap Fitzpatrick as a DB1 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Dane Belton showed up in Week 4, recording six solos, eight assists, and one pass defended. It was the first spike week for Belton, who has been solid for fantasy managers, registering four or more solos in three straight contests. Tap Belton as a top-30 type as long as he is starting and producing.

Grant Delpit showed up in Week 4, racking up four solos, two assists,  one interception, and one pass defended. Delpit has been inconsistent but has two spike weeks to his name in four weeks of action, keeping him in the mix as an upside DB3 play. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup against the New York Jets.

Reed Blankenship was excellent in Week 4, generating five solos and six assists. Reed has recorded five or more solos in two straight games and checks into Week 5 as the DB18, thanks to back-to-back spike weeks. Count Blankenship as a top-25 option as long as he is producing.

Amik Robertson was excellent in Week 4, racking up seven solos, two assists, and one pass defended. The DB8/CB2 through four weeks of action, Robertson is a must-start DB3/CB1 play as long as he stays hot. Amik has posted three straight 'spike' weeks with four or more solos in each. Count him as a top-36 option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants.

C.J. Henderson went off again in Week 4, exploding with nine solos, one assist, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended. The former first-round pick has looked like just that since stepping in for the injured AJ Terrell and likely made himself quite a bit of money with his dominant two-game stretch. He is hard to project for IDP, but he is too hot to ignore while he is sizzling. Fresh off an eight solo, three passes defended Week 3, Henderson should be tapped as a flex option while he is producing at an elite level. Act accordingly for Week 5.

Justin Walley stayed liquid in Week 4, racking up five solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Walley has already recorded two games with five solos, offering fantasy managers steady tackle production with a pass defended usually in the offing as well. Tap Walley as a CB1 option while he is cooking, with an eye on potentially utilizing the slot corner as a DB3 option as we get deeper into the byes.

Jacob Parrish stepped up in Week 4, tallying five solos, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Parrish has registered back-to-back games with four or more solos, putting him squarely in the CB2 mix. Parrish is not someone those in 12-team leagues without dedicated CB slots should be paying much attention to. Add him to watch lists but look elsewhere for Week 5.

Jourdan Lewis showed up in Week 4, racking up three solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Lewis has recorded two spike weeks so far but remains more of a CB league option, at least for now. He is an easy CB1 play but remains more DB4/flex than DB3, at least for now. Treat him as such for a plus Week 5 matchup.

Deonte Banks returned to action with a bang for the New York Giants, recording one solo, three assists, one interception, four passes defended, and one touchdown. Banks has been impressive in his two starts this season and belongs on the CB2 radar. He will need to show some more consistency before we can start trusting him as a DB3 or CB1 option, but he has certainly flashed the upside to project his inclusion in that conversation in the near future. For now, though, keep counting him as a CB2/DB5 and look elsewhere for your Week 5 DB3.

Jarrian Jones was at it again in Week 4, generating seven solos, one tackle for loss, and three passes defended. Jarrian has now posted back-to-back spike weeks, forcing his way into the CB2 discussion in the process. Jones has seen over 70 percent of the snaps over the last three weeks, and while he is currently better known for his violent facemask on Ja'Marr Chase, he is a burgeoning IDP asset in CB leagues who belongs on deeper DB league radars as well. Treat him as a top-25 CB option for a plus Week 5 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Rayuan Lane stepped up in Week 4, tallying six solos, two assists, and one pass defended on 57 percent of the snaps. Lane saw an expanded role with both Eric Murray and Caleb Ransaw going down with injuries and responded with a DB2-level fantasy outing and a key stop on Chase Brown. Lane is a Week 5 option with Murray ultimately expected to be ruled out for the Jaguars' annual London game. Keep him on the radar as a potential DB3/flex option.
